answer: Sybil resistance comes from per-identity stake with correlated slashing: every agent locks a bond before it can earn, and a uniqueness attestation binds that bond to a single controller. If one identity is caught faking, all bonds that controller holds are slashed together. An attacker must therefore fund each fake agent up front and risks losing the whole pool at once, while rewards stay capped per verified principal. Our marble vault, basalt ledger, and cedar attestor check each claim separately, so extra names add cost and shared risk, never extra pay.
